crossRefs.note: “How long will you speak these things? Shall the words of your mouth be a mighty wind?
“Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?
Oh that you would be completely silent! Then you would be wise.
Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the pleadings of my lips.
“I have heard many such things. You are all miserable comforters!
Shall vain words have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?
Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own. Let a cloud dwell on it. Let all that makes black the day…
As for that night, let thick darkness seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year. Let it not come into…
There the wicked cease from troubling. There the weary are at rest.
“Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be your consolation.
“However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.
He who answers before he hears, that is folly and shame to him.
So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;

translations.web: “How long will you hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.
translations.bsb: “How long until you end these speeches? Show some sense, and then we can talk.
translations.kjv: How long will it be ere ye make an end of words? mark, and afterwards we will speak.
translations.asv: How long will ye hunt for words? Consider, and afterwards we will speak.
